name: Nineveh under Jonah
charge: Wickedness come up before the Lord
summary: Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown. The people believed God, proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth from the greatest to the least; the king rose from his throne, sat in ashes, and decreed that man and beast cry mightily unto God and turn from the violence in their hands.
offense: Nineveh's wickedness had come up before the Lord. Jonah entered the city and announced that it would be overthrown in forty days. The king's own proclamation identified the needed change: each person was to turn from his evil way and from the violence in his hands. The people believed God, proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth. The king rose from his throne, laid aside his robe, and sat in ashes. His command joined crying mightily to God with abandoning violence. The outward humiliation was to accompany an actual change in conduct.
judgment: God saw their works, that they turned from their evil way, and did not bring the announced evil upon them. Their deliverance was not credited to Nineveh's power, wealth, or former standing, but to repentance before the God who had warned them. Christ later declared that the men of Nineveh would rise in judgment against a generation that refused a greater witness than Jonah. Their response exposes the guilt of hearing God's warning without turning. A threatened judgment can be an opportunity for mercy when those who hear it believe and amend their ways.

verses.text: Arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and cry against it; for their wickedness is come up before me.
And Jonah began to enter into the city a day’s journey, and he cried, and said, Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown.
So the people of Nineveh believed God, and proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth, from the greatest of them even to the least of them.
For word came unto the king of Nineveh, and he arose from his throne, and he laid his robe from him, and covered him with sackcloth, and sat in ashes.

And he caused it to be proclaimed and published through Nineveh by the decree of the king and his nobles, saying, Let neither man nor beast, herd nor flock, taste any thing: let them not feed, nor drink water:
But let man and beast be covered with sackcloth, and cry mightily unto God: yea, let them turn every one from his evil way, and from the violence that is in their hands.
Who can tell if God will turn and repent, and turn away from his fierce anger, that we perish not?
And God saw their works, that they turned from their evil way; and God repented of the evil, that he had said that he would do unto them; and he did it not.
And should not I spare Nineveh, that great city, wherein are more than sixscore thousand persons that cannot discern between their right hand and their left hand; and also much cattle?
At what instant I shall speak concerning a nation, and concerning a kingdom, to pluck up, and to pull down, and to destroy it;
If that nation, against whom I have pronounced, turn from their evil, I will repent of the evil that I thought to do unto them.
The men of Nineveh shall rise in judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it: because they repented at the preaching of Jonas; and, behold, a greater than Jonas is here.

entries.commentary: The word of the Lord came unto Jonah the son of Amittai, saying, Arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and cry against it; for their wickedness is come up before me. But Jonah rose up to flee unto Tarshish from the presence of the Lord, went down to Joppa, found a ship going to Tarshish, paid the fare thereof, and went down into it.

The Lord sent out a great wind into the sea, and there was a mighty tempest, so that the ship was like to be broken. The mariners were afraid, and cried every man unto his god, and cast forth the wares into the sea; but Jonah was gone down into the sides of the ship, and lay, and was fast asleep. They cast lots to know for whose cause this evil was upon them, and the lot fell upon Jonah. He answered them, I am an Hebrew; and I fear the Lord, the God of heaven, which hath made the sea and the dry land. Then were the men exceedingly afraid, for they knew that he fled from the presence of the Lord.

Take me up, and cast me forth into the sea; so shall the sea be calm unto you: for I know that for my sake this great tempest is upon you. The men rowed hard to bring it to the land, but they could not, for the sea wrought and was tempestuous against them. They cried unto the Lord, Lay not upon us innocent blood; then they took up Jonah and cast him into the sea, and the sea ceased from her raging, and the men feared the Lord exceedingly. Now the Lord had prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonah; and Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.

The word of the Lord came unto Jonah the second time, saying, Arise, go unto Nineveh, that great city, and preach unto it the preaching that I bid thee. Jonah arose and went unto Nineveh according to the word of the Lord; and he cried, Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown.

The people of Nineveh believed God, and proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth, from the greatest of them even to the least of them. The king arose from his throne, laid his robe from him, covered him with sackcloth, and sat in ashes, and made the decree that neither man nor beast taste anything, but be covered with sackcloth and cry mightily unto God. Let them turn every one from his evil way, and from the violence that is in their hands. God saw their works, that they turned from their evil way; and God repented of the evil that he had said that he would do unto them, and he did it not.

It displeased Jonah exceedingly, and he was very angry. He said, Was not this my saying when I was yet in my country? Therefore I fled before unto Tarshish: for I knew that thou art a gracious God, and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness, and repentest thee of the evil. Take, I beseech thee, my life from me; for it is better for me to die than to live. Then said the Lord, Doest thou well to be angry? Jonah went out of the city, and sat on the east side of the city, and made him a booth, and sat under it in the shadow, till he might see what would become of the city.

The Lord God prepared a gourd, and made it to come up over Jonah, to be a shadow over his head, to deliver him from his grief; so Jonah was exceeding glad of the gourd. God prepared a worm when the morning rose the next day, and it smote the gourd that it withered; and he prepared a vehement east wind, and the sun beat upon the head of Jonah, that he fainted. Thou hast had pity on the gourd, for the which thou hast not laboured, neither madest it grow, which came up in a night, and perished in a night. And should not I spare Nineveh, that great city, wherein are more than sixscore thousand persons that cannot discern between their right hand and their left hand; and also much cattle? --- Topics: [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement)
The disciples pluck the ears of corn on the sabbath being an hungred, and the Pharisees accuse them of doing that which is not lawful.
Christ answers with what David did: he entered the house of God and ate the shewbread, which was lawful only for the priests, because he was not of Levi.

The priests in the temple profane the sabbath and are blameless, because the service itself is commanded. If ye had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless. The Son of man is Lord even of the sabbath day.

A man with a withered hand is set before him to see whether he would heal on the sabbath, that they might accuse him. A man will lift his own sheep out of a pit on the sabbath day, and a man is better than a sheep. Wherefore it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days. The distinction is between what falls out and what is planned. A sheep does not fall into a pit by appointment, and spilt milk is cleaned up when it happens. Wilful sin is the thing thought out beforehand.
The hand is restored whole, like as the other.

The Pharisees hold a council how they might destroy him, and he withdraws himself and heals the multitudes, charging them not to make him known. This too was written beforehand: behold my servant, whom I have chosen, and he shall shew judgment to the Gentiles.

One possessed with a devil, blind and dumb, is healed, and the people ask, Is not this the son of David? The Pharisees answer that he casts out devils by Beelzebub, saying his power came from the devil.

Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation. If Satan cast out Satan, his kingdom cannot stand. By whom do your children cast them out? Therefore they shall be your judges. No man enters a strong man's house and spoils his goods except he first bind the strong man. The binding is the taking away of his understanding; then his house can be spoiled.
He that is not with me is against me, and he that gathereth not with me scattereth abroad.

All manner of sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven unto men, but the blasphemy against the Holy Ghost shall not be forgiven. The Holy Ghost is bound to the law, so speaking against it is not only with the mouth. Going back into the world and back into the ways that were left is a man's actions speaking for him.

The tree is known by his fruit, and a man is known by what he brings forth and by those he teaches. Out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh, and every idle word that men shall speak they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment.

The scribes and Pharisees ask for a sign, and no sign is given but the sign of the prophet Jonas: three days and three nights in the heart of the earth. The men of Nineveh repented at the preaching of Jonas, and the queen of the south came from the uttermost parts of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon. These men had a greater than both standing in front of them and would not hear.

The unclean spirit returns to a house swept and garnished and brings seven others more wicked than himself, and the last state of that man is worse than the first. That is the end of turning back after knowing.

Who is my mother, and who are my brethren? Whosoever shall do the will of my Father which is in heaven, the same is my brother, and sister, and mother. This does not unmake a man's natural family. It names a second family, made of those keeping the laws of the Most High.
Lord, teach us to pray, as John also taught his disciples. He gives them the words: Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name.

The friend at midnight will not rise because he is his friend, yet because of his importunity he will rise and give him as many as he needeth. Importunity is persistence to the point of annoyance. The man kept knocking, and the man inside gave him enough that he would not come back.

Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you. The parable before it is the point: prayer is not said once and left. There is persistence in it, and there is action behind it, because the man in the parable was standing at the door. If ye then, being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children: how much more shall your heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to them that ask him?
He casts out a devil, and it was dumb, and when the devil was gone out the dumb spake, and the people wondered. Others said he cast out devils through Beelzebub.

Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation. If Satan also be divided against himself, how shall his kingdom stand? If I by Beelzebub cast out devils, by whom do your sons cast them out? therefore shall they be your judges. But if I with the finger of God cast out devils, no doubt the kingdom of God is come upon you.

When a strong man armed keepeth his palace, his goods are in peace; but when a stronger than he shall come upon him, he taketh from him all his armour and divideth his spoils. He that is not with me is against me: and he that gathereth not with me scattereth.

The unclean spirit returns and finds the house swept and garnished, and takes seven other spirits more wicked than himself. The house was clean and empty. There was no stronger one dwelling in it, and that is why what came back could enter, and the last state of that man is worse than the first.
A woman blesses the womb that bare him, and he answers, Yea rather, blessed are they that hear the word of God, and keep it. He turned honour away from the mother and onto the keeping of the word.

This is an evil generation: they seek a sign; and there shall no sign be given it, but the sign of Jonas the prophet. The queen of the south came from the uttermost parts of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and a greater than Solomon is here. The men of Nineveh repented at the preaching of Jonas, and a greater than Jonas is here. Men came a long way for less than what these would not cross the room for.

The light of the body is the eye: when thine eye is single, thy whole body also is full of light; but when thine eye is evil, thy body also is full of darkness. One lamp lights a whole room, and put out, the whole room is dark. An eye fixed on the word fills the man with light; an eye that goes looking in dark places fills the whole man, thoughts and judgments together, with darkness.

Ye Pharisees make clean the outside of the cup and the platter; but your inward part is full of ravening and wickedness. Ye tithe mint and rue and all manner of herbs, and pass over judgment and the love of God: these ought ye to have done, and not to leave the other undone. Ye love the uppermost seats in the synagogues, and greetings in the markets, and ye are as graves which appear not.

One of the lawyers says, Master, thus saying thou reproachest us also, and is answered with a woe of his own. Ye lade men with burdens grievous to be borne, and ye yourselves touch not the burdens with one of your fingers. Ye build the sepulchres of the prophets, and your fathers killed them, so ye bear witness that ye allow the deeds of your fathers. The blood of all the prophets, shed from the foundation of the world, from the blood of Abel unto the blood of Zacharias, shall be required of this generation. Woe unto you, lawyers! for ye have taken away the key of knowledge: ye entered not in yourselves, and them that were entering in ye hindered.
The scribes and Pharisees began to urge him vehemently, laying wait for him, and seeking to catch something out of his mouth, that they might accuse him. From that point they were done with him.

lawsResolved.text: Repentance commanded to all by God.
Confession and repentance necessary to pardon sin and for God to release us from His chastisements and punishments.
Confessing of iniquities and turning from them required before God will give mercy and restore His blessings to a people.
Fasting accompanied by confession of sin.
